title: There is one real reason to book the ship's tour.
subtitle: It is not the guiding, the coach or the commentary. It is who pays when the traffic doesn't move.

text: A late ship's excursion is the line's problem. A late private tour is yours.
sub: On the cruise line's own excursion, the ship waits — or the line is responsible for getting you to the next port at its cost. Independently, it is not required to wait at all.

right.label: Ship's tour
items: Ship holds, or the line arranges
You rejoin at the next port

title: Three port days where I book through the ship

items.head: The site is over an hour inland
items.body: Ephesus, Pompeii, the Douro terraces. Distance is what removes your ability to recover a delay.

items.head: It is a tendered call
items.body: Add the tender queue at both ends and a comfortable margin becomes no margin at all.

items.head: A short call, or a border crossing
items.body: Under seven hours alongside, or any day that ends with a passport check, and I stop being clever about it.

kicker: And the rest of the week
text: On a long call in a walkable port, hire your own guide.
sub: Ten hours in Dubrovnik or Bordeaux is not a day that needs institutional protection. That is where a private guide earns every pound of the difference.

quote: Knowing which days have no margin is the job. The excursion choice follows from that, not the other way round.

title: Send this to whoever books your shore days
body: Send me your itinerary and I'll mark the two or three days where the ship's tour is the correct answer — and the rest, where it plainly isn't.
